overall: Los Angeles is under a firm marine layer this morning, with temperatures locked in a remarkably tight band of 62.1–63.0°F from midnight through at least 08:20 ET (05:20 PT) — essentially zero warming overnight. High dewpoints (~57°F) and light southwesterly winds confirm the coastal marine influence. The NWS expects patchy fog to persist until around 11am PT, with a mostly cloudy afternoon, suggesting any afternoon warm-up will be moderated.
forecast_obs_notes: NWP models cluster reasonably tightly: ECMWF at 68.2°F, HRRR at 69.5°F, and NBM at 67.0°F — a 2.5°F spread with a consensus center around 68°F. The NWS official forecast of 69°F aligns with the upper end of that range. The intraday bucket distribution skews notably higher (peak probability mass in the 74–79°F range), which appears inconsistent with the NWP consensus; this likely reflects model uncertainty given the very flat early-morning profile rather than a genuine signal for higher temps.
max_temp_prediction: The most likely outcome is a TMAX in the 67–69°F range, consistent with the NWP model average (~68°F) and the NWS 69°F forecast. The persistent marine layer and 'mostly cloudy' afternoon sky will cap the warm-up even after fog clears. If the marine layer lingers deeper into the afternoon than forecast, the high could fall short of 68°F; if it scours out earlier, 69–70°F is possible but would require clearing ahead of schedule. Confidence is moderate-high in the 67–69°F window, with the central estimate near 68°F. Active weather alerts (fire weather, extreme heat) all affect inland desert and mountain zones far from coastal LA and are not a meaningful driver here.
